newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan c.bank chief says currency safe from attack.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan c.bank chief says currency safe from attack.

text.p: Central bank chief Hsu Yuan-dong said on Wednesday that Taiwan's huge reserves and trade surplus helped to insulate its currency from speculative attacks like those that have undermined currencies in southeast Asia.

"Our situation is different from that in southeast Asia," Hsu told reporters. "We have big foreign exchange reserves and a big trade surplus. Our economy is good. What happened in southeast Asia cannot happen here. We won't have any problem."
The central bank governor's comment was his most explicit comment to date on the speculative pressures that have undermined several southeast Asian currencies in July.
On Wednesday, the Taiwan dollar closed at an eight-year low against its U.S. counterpart, reflecting the strength of the greenback in Tokyo and other overseas markets, dealers said.
The local dollar dipped as low as T$27.958 before ending at T$27.939 against Tuesday's T$27.925 close.
Dealers reported seeing apparent central bank intervention in late trade, especially in the final minute, to slow the Taiwan dollar's depreciation.
